title: Grade 11 Physics — Gravitation
description: Newton's law of gravitation, gravitational field, escape velocity, orbital motion
subject: physics

questions.question: Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation states the force between two masses m₁ and m₂ separated by distance r is:
questions.explanation: F = Gm₁m₂/r². G = 6.67×10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg² (Universal Gravitational Constant). Force is attractive, acts along the line joining the masses, and follows the inverse square law.

questions.question: The acceleration due to gravity at the surface of Earth (g) is:
questions.explanation: g = GM/R² where M = Earth's mass, R = Earth's radius. g ≈ 9.8 m/s² at surface. At height h: g' = g(R/(R+h))². At depth d: g' = g(1 − d/R).

questions.question: Escape velocity from Earth's surface is approximately:
questions.explanation: Escape velocity v_e = √(2gR) = √(2GM/R) ≈ 11.2 km/s. This is the minimum speed needed to escape Earth's gravity. Orbital speed = 7.9 km/s (for low orbit).

questions.question: Kepler's Third Law states: T² ∝ ?
questions.explanation: Kepler's Third Law: T² ∝ a³ (period squared is proportional to cube of semi-major axis). T²/a³ = constant for all planets orbiting the same star. Derived from gravitational force = centripetal force.

questions.question: Gravitational potential energy between two masses is:
questions.explanation: U = −GMm/r. Negative because: work is done by gravity when masses approach (energy released). U = 0 at r = ∞. As r decreases, U becomes more negative (energy released/binding energy increases).

questions.question: A geostationary satellite orbits at approximately:
options: 36,000 km (with T = 24 h, rotates with Earth)
questions.explanation: Geostationary orbit: ~36,000 km above equator, period = 24 hours. The satellite appears stationary relative to Earth. Used for communication, weather, GPS. Must be in equatorial plane.

questions.question: Weightlessness in a satellite is because:
options: There is no gravity in space
The satellite and astronaut are both in free fall — both fall at the same acceleration
The satellite moves too fast for gravity to act
Gravity is balanced by centrifugal force in the satellite's frame
questions.explanation: In orbit, both the satellite and everything inside are in free fall — they accelerate toward Earth at the same rate (g_orbit). There is no normal force → apparent weightlessness. Gravity still acts!

questions.question: The orbital velocity of a satellite at radius r from Earth's centre is:
questions.explanation: Setting gravitational force = centripetal force: GMm/r² = mv²/r → v = √(GM/r). Note: escape velocity = √(2GM/R) = √2 × orbital velocity at surface.

questions.question: Gravitational field strength at a point is defined as:
options: The force between any two masses
Force per unit mass (g = F/m) — acceleration due to gravity at that point
questions.explanation: Gravitational field strength g = F/m = GM/r². It is the force experienced per unit mass placed at that point. Units: N/kg = m/s². Also equal to acceleration due to gravity.

questions.question: g at a height h above Earth's surface is approximately (for h << R):
questions.explanation: g' = GM/(R+h)² ≈ g(1 − 2h/R) for h << R (binomial approximation). Exact: g' = g×R²/(R+h)². g decreases with altitude.

questions.question: Kepler's Second Law (equal areas in equal times) is a consequence of:
questions.explanation: Kepler's 2nd Law: a planet sweeps equal areas in equal intervals of time. This results from conservation of angular momentum — gravity provides no torque (force along r), so L = mr²ω = constant.

questions.question: The gravitational potential at distance r from mass M is:
questions.explanation: Gravitational potential V = −GM/r (per unit mass). Note: GPE = mV = −GMm/r. Potential is always negative (energy must be added to move mass to infinity). V increases (becomes less negative) with distance.

questions.question: If Earth were to shrink to half its radius while mass stays the same, g at the surface would:
questions.explanation: g = GM/R². If R → R/2: g_new = GM/(R/2)² = GM × 4/R² = 4g. Quadruples. This is why white dwarfs and neutron stars have enormous surface gravity despite similar or smaller mass than sun.

questions.question: The total energy of a satellite in circular orbit is:
questions.explanation: Total energy E = KE + PE = ½mv² + (−GMm/r) = GMm/2r − GMm/r = −GMm/2r (negative = bound state). To escape, you need to add energy to make E = 0.

questions.question: Gravitational force is always:
options: Attractive — mass always attracts mass (no negative mass)
Both attractive and repulsive depending on charge
questions.explanation: Gravity is ALWAYS attractive — unlike electric/magnetic forces, there is no 'antigravity'. Gravitational force becomes very small at large distances (∝1/r²) but never exactly zero.
